Alerts & Events

Asset Events

📄 Version 1.0 👤 Audience: Technical Support / Installation Team

Asset Events are a set of conditions, per Asset, that trigger events. Events can be used to generate Alerts. For example, if a vehicle speeds, a temperature reading goes too high, a fuel level has a sudden drop, or a driver over-revs the engine — those are all events. Alerts use those events to sound the alarm or notify someone of the issue. These triggers/events can be edited on Assets individually, or in bulk.

1. Finding & Editing Asset Event Triggers

Individual Assets

1Go to Administration
2Choose the Assets section under the Client
3Choose the Asset you would like to edit from the list
4Choose the Events section on the Asset
5Click the Edit button on the section you would like to edit

Multiple Assets (Bulk)

1Go to Administration
2Choose the Assets section under the Client
3Choose the Assets you would like to edit from the list (Ctrl-click on more than one Asset)
4Choose the Events section on the Assets
5Click the Edit button on the section you would like to edit
Please note: any information already in the sections will disappear, and any changes made will affect all the Assets chosen.

After clicking the Edit button, choose which Trigger to add. As per the example below, we are adding Analog Triggers:

1Click Add under the Analogs section — a pop-up appears with Analog Event Triggers
2Choose the Analog IO you would like to create events from
3Add the Min and Max Range (if one of the limits is not needed, add a number that will never trigger an event), the Range Debounce (see below), and Drop and Increase amount, depending on the Input
Range Debounce = the number of positions the drop or increase needs to be over, for the event to trigger. For example, if Range Debounce = 6, the drop or increase needs to be constant over 6 packets of data.

2. Event Triggers — Speed & Idle

Speed

The platform uses the lower of map road speed limits, location speed limit, and Asset Event Triggers (Max Speed and Tolerance) to generate Speeding events. The platform applies the lower limit, with the tolerance added on, as the working speed limit.

The platform does not know what type of vehicle you are tracking — it could be a Caterpillar Grader, a 10-Ton Truck, or a High Performance car. Each vehicle has different maximum speeds allowed, and map road speed limits may not apply equally to all of them.

Example: a Caterpillar Grader may be set to a maximum of 30 with 0% tolerance, and would be speeding at any speed above 31 — regardless of whether the road speed limit is 40, 50, or higher. Any speed limit above 30 is ignored in this case. Set these values as required, per Asset, either individually or in bulk.

In the example below, the following speeds would be considered speeding (11% above the map speed limit):

Map or Location Speed LimitSpeeding Event Triggers At
4045

8089

120133

In the example below, the following would be considered speeding:

Idling

The platform generates an Excessive Idling event using the value set on the Asset/s. If the Asset idles for longer than the limit set, an event triggers, which can then be used to generate an Alert. Set this value according to the Asset being monitored.

3. Event Triggers — Working Hours

Working hours can be added to an Asset, which allows Users three outputs:

1Curfew Violations — an Alert can be generated when an Asset is used outside of working hours
2Curfew Violation Report — generates the trips taken outside of working hours, in Listing or Daily Summary format, like the Trip Listing Reports
3Asset Utilisation Report — determines utilisation statistics within working hours, including distance, idling, and active time

After clicking the Edit button next to Working Hours:

1Click Add under the Curfews section — a pop-up appears
2Set the Time of day the hours should start and end
3Set the Time Zone
4Set the Days of the week the hours need to apply to
5Click OK when the information is correct

Add the hours per day, and repeat if there is more than one set of working hours. For example, if Assets can be used from 08h00–17h00 during the week and 09h00–13h00 on a Saturday, create two sets of working hours — one for the week, and one for Saturday.

Please note: the “day” ends at 23:59. If an Asset works overnight (e.g. 18h00 to 06h00), create one set of working hours from 18h00–23h59, and a second set from 00h00–06h00.

4. Event Triggers — Analog Triggers

Analog triggers include all Analog, CAN, and Temperature values coming from the Device. The data from the Device can be used to trigger the following events:

1Low range event — when the data value drops below this level
2High range event — when the data value rises above this level
3Drop event — when the data value drops quickly
4Increase event — when the data value increases quickly

Examples include:

RPMValue too high = over-revving
TemperatureValue too high or too low = out of acceptable range for goods in transit
Fuel LevelValue drops quickly = possible fuel theft
Fuel LevelValue rises quickly = fuel fill-up

If you would like to trigger an event when an Asset crosses a specific Zone boundary, or a State/Province or Country border, set this up under Geographic Triggers:

6. Event Triggers — Trip Limits (Driver Fatigue)

If you would like to trigger events for “Driver Fatigue” or “Trip Limits”, set these up under the following:

Maximum Trip DistanceThe distance after which an event will be generated
Maximum Trip TimeThe time after which an event will be generated whilst the Asset is in a trip (Ignition On)
Maximum Inactive TimeThe time after which an event will be triggered when an Asset is not moving

Once these parameters are defined, you can set up Alerts for Assets that are moving for extended periods without resting, moving long distances without turning off the ignition, and stationary for extended periods.

7. Creating Alerts from Event Triggers

To create an Alert from Event Triggers, set up the rest of the Alert as normal, and choose the type of Range or change event from the following options:

1Select action...
2Analog/CAN Violations = Analog and/or CAN triggers
3Border Crossing = Geographic triggers
4Excessive Idle = Idling limit trigger
5Overspeed = Speeding triggers
6Temperature Violation = Analog trigger for temperature
